During #903's review, 2 of 8 dispatched Step-3 lens agents violated
`plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s status-line-first rule — each led with a

  the status-line instruction to be even more prominent), or add a mechanical check the dispatcher
  is instructed to run against every subagent reply before treating its content as valid (does the
  literal first line match the required vocabulary exactly).
- Consider whether `friction-events.js`'s existing `contract-violation` detection could be
  surfaced back to the dispatching agent in-run (rather than only visible via a later
  Friction-lens reflect pass), closing the loop faster.

## Acceptance Criteria

   `contract-violation` events, OR every violation triggers an actual re-prompt per the contract's
   existing (but unenforced) rule.

# Ledger item 19 (from #903 review, reflect hindsight evaluation 5)

**Origin:** ledger resolve gate, spec #903 review/hindsight
**Defer-reason:** tangential

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:reflect` hindsight mode (invoked during #903's review) surfaced a general,
reusable pattern: a mechanized deterministic check that parses loose, real-world prose (not a
formal grammar) needs an explicit could-not-parse signal, never a silent `null`/skip that
collapses into a false negative. This is the exact shape of #903's own ledger item 18 (Check C's
`parseStep2`), but the lesson generalizes beyond plan-audit — any future "mechanize a hand-run
prose check" work in this repo is at risk of the same failure mode. No existing project skill
under `.claude/skills/` obviously covers this general lesson (the closest, `gh-api-module-pattern`,
is scoped to `gh`/`git`-shelling CLI conventions, not parser API design).

## Deliverables

- Either a new short section in an existing relevant skill, or a small new skill, stating the
  rule: when mechanizing a prose heuristic into a deterministic check, the "couldn't parse this
  input" case must be a distinguishable return value/signal, never silently identical to "this
  input legitimately doesn't apply."
- Cite #903's `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/parser.js` `parseStep2` as the worked example.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reader of the target skill can find this guidance when writing a new mechanized/deterministic
   check over free-form text.
2. The guidance names the concrete anti-pattern (collapsing "doesn't apply" and "couldn't parse"
   into one `null`/skip) and the concrete fix shape (a distinguishable signal + a surfaced warning).

## Current State

`assess-agent-autonomy/merge-check.md` Step 1 resolves `INTEGRATION_BRANCH` per `_shared/integration-branch.md`, which (inside a worktree) correctly falls back to the bare GitHub-default branch name, e.g. `"main"`, and passes that bare name straight to `blast-radius.js --integration-branch`.

`review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 2 already carries an explicit guard against exactly this class of hazard for its own `{base}` resolution: "never trust a bare local branch name for `{base}`... resolve it via `git fetch origin {base}` then use `origin/{base}`." `merge-check.md`'s Step 1 has no equivalent instruction before invoking `blast-radius.js`.

Observed live during a `/claude-tweaks:review` merge-check for record #897: the shared checkout's local `main` ref was stale (`b3962148`, well behind `origin/main` at `0efccfdf2`). `blast-radius.js --integration-branch main` resolved the merge base against the stale local ref and reported a wildly inflated blast radius (`implLines=1071`, `implFiles=35`, covering ~38 unrelated commits) instead of the record's actual 6-file/127-line diff. `blast-radius.js --integration-branch origin/main` gave the correct numbers. Caught only because the numbers looked implausible for the record's known scope — a less obviously-wrong stale-branch read could silently produce a false `needs-human` (or worse, a false `auto-merge`) verdict.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Either (a) `merge-check.md`'s Step 1 applies the same fetch-and-prefer-origin discipline `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 2 already states before calling `blast-radius.js`, or (b) `blast-radius.js` itself resolves `--integration-branch {name}` against `origin/{name}` when that ref exists, falling back to the bare local ref only if it doesn't — the second option fixes every caller (`assess-agent-autonomy`, `residue.js` already defaults to `origin/main` per its own doc note, so this would make the two consistent) at once rather than just this one call site.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A shared checkout with a stale local `main` (behind `origin/main`) produces the same blast-radius numbers whether `--integration-branch main` or `--integration-branch origin/main` is passed.
2. A test pins the stale-local-branch scenario (fixture repo with local `main` behind a remote-tracking `origin/main`) and asserts the resolved merge base matches `origin/main`'s, not the stale local ref's.

# Reflect — staged finding 2

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light from #1410
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Record #1410 and record #1402 (PR #1577, parked/unmerged) both diagnose the exact same root
cause in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js`'s `resolveRun` fallback branches — a missing
worktree-binding check. #1402's build ran first but its PR never merged; #1410 was later
authorized and dispatched, and its own build necessarily re-implemented the identical fix from
scratch (it had no way to build on top of #1402's unmerged branch). Direct diff comparison during
#1410's review confirmed the two PRs' functional code is byte-identical in `context.js`, differing
only in explanatory-comment wording — a trivial, but real, merge conflict on second-merge (also
touching one `docs/hooks.md` line both PRs edit differently). Nothing detected this duplication
before dispatch authorized and ran #1410's build; it only surfaced because this review call
happened to cross-reference the two PRs by hand at the operator's explicit request.

## Deliverables

- `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` (or `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`, wherever authorization happens)
  gains a check that flags — at authorization or dispatch time, not discovered post-hoc in review —
  when two `ready`/`auto:build` records name overlapping file regions or an unmerged sibling PR
  already claims to fix the same root cause, so a human can choose to serialize them (block #1410
  on #1402's merge) rather than pay for two independent builds of the same fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A concrete detection signal is proposed (file-overlap on unmerged PR diffs, a shared

While performing #1313's final whole-branch review (fix compute-then-exit truncation risk in `plugin/bin/release.js` and `plugin/bin/review-coordination.js` — itself a follow-up to #1176's earlier sweep), the reviewer found that #1313's own sweep enumeration was incomplete. `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js:76` carries the identical idiom:

```js
process.exit(run(process.argv.slice(2)));
```

`run()`'s `build`/`mint` branches end with `deps.stdout(JSON.stringify(result) + '\n'); return 0;` — the same shape #1176/#1313 already fixed elsewhere: a stdout write immediately before returning an integer that then feeds `process.exit()`, which can truncate the write for a piped consumer.

A GitHub search (`gh issue list --search "build-review-context process.exit"` and `--search "truncation exit in:title"`, both `--state all`) found no existing record for this file.

Surface: backend

## Overview

Enforcement-layer half of the #965 run-state ownership hardening (parent record has the full rationale): the two inline `owner !== caller` session-id comparisons in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`, and `resolveRun`'s session-scoped `attribution: 'session'` path in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js`, all assume session id ≡ actor. Because `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is shared across all subagents of a session (measured 2026-08-20, #965), a sibling agent in its own worktree is misclassified as the run's own session: the E-checks take the same-session branch (deny) instead of the foreign branch (warn/allow + event), and `resolveRun` confidently returns a sibling's run as the caller's own. These fail toward deny/warn rather than corruption — lower stakes than the mutating verbs — but they are the same broken equivalence and complete the ownership contract.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 5

## Non-Goals

- No change to any hooks.js mutating verb — that is the mutating-verbs sibling sub-issue (#1012).
- No change to which E-checks exist, their deny/warn/allow outcomes per classification, or their event vocabulary (`wd-foreign-teardown`, `wd-foreign-session`, `wd-deny`, `wd-push-mismatch`) — only how "foreign" is decided.
- Not implementing #607's deliverables (fallback-attribution breadcrumb hygiene) — #607 stays independent; this unit only touches the `attribution: 'session'` arm, not the `'fallback'` arm #607 targets.
- No change to the sanctioned console-execution exception documented at `resolveRun`'s header.

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| #1098 | hooks context: add classifyOwnership | open |

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — two sites compare `state.sessionId` against the hook payload's `ctx.input.session_id`. Teardown path: `if (owner && caller && owner !== caller)` → foreign branch (allow + `wd-foreign-teardown` event + warning); everything else — same-session, unowned target, or missing identity on either side — falls through to one deny. Commit path: the same `owner && caller && owner !== caller` guard → foreign branch (allow + `wd-foreign-session` event + systemMessage); everything else, missing-identity cases included, falls through to `wd-deny` (confirmed against the code — the missing-identity case has no separate branch today; "preserve existing behavior" for `indeterminate` means landing in these same fall-throughs). The hook payload's `session_id` is the same shared session identity as the env var. The teardown site classifies the **target** run (`hit.state`, found by worktree path); the commit site classifies the caller's **own resolved** run (`ctx.runState`) — pass each site its own `state` object.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `resolveRun(cwd, env, sessionId)`: with a known session id, returns the first run whose `state.sessionId === me` as `attribution: 'session'`; under shared ids the first such run may be a sibling's. `classifyOwnership` (prerequisite sub-issue): verify the shipped signature and verdict strings against that record's Data / API Surface table at build start, before writing any call.
- Tests: the pinning surface for existing behavior is `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` plus every suite exercising `resolveRun` — `hooks-run-arg-anchoring.test.js`, `hooks-run-attribution.test.js`, `hooks-context.test.js`, `hooks-dispatcher.test.js`, `teardown-gate.test.js`, `skill-invocation.test.js`, `hooks-spec-status.test.js`, `wrap-up-engine-run-dir-anchoring.test.js` (enumerated by `grep -rl "resolveRun" tests/`; re-run the grep at build time in case the list moved).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Both `pre-tool-use.js` comparison sites decide foreign-vs-own via `classifyOwnership({ sessionId: ctx.input.session_id, cwd: ctx.cwd }, state)` instead of raw id equality: verdict `foreign` takes the existing foreign branch, `mine` the existing same-session branch, `indeterminate` preserves each site's current missing-identity behavior (teardown path: deny; commit path: fall through to `wd-deny`) — outcome semantics per classification unchanged, only the classifier swapped.
- [ ] `resolveRun`'s session-scoped loop skips a run whose `classifyOwnership` verdict against the caller is `foreign` (sibling's bound run) instead of returning it as `attribution: 'session'`. **Only `foreign` skips**: an `indeterminate` verdict (e.g. the recorded worktree is unresolvable) keeps today's behavior and is still returned as `attribution: 'session'` — fail-open, and what keeps single-session resolution byte-identical. "Single-session" here means: no non-terminal run bound to a live worktree other than the caller's own under the same session id — in that scope, order and results are unchanged.
- [ ] Pinning tests: (a) existing single-session scenarios in the hooks suites pass unchanged — zero edits to existing assertions; (b) new cases: same session id + caller cwd in worktree A vs a run bound to worktree B → teardown path classifies foreign (allow + `wd-foreign-teardown`), commit path classifies foreign (allow + `wd-foreign-session`), `resolveRun` skips the sibling run and falls through to its unowned/null result.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A sibling agent (identical session id, own worktree) tearing down or committing against another sibling's bound run takes the foreign branch at both `pre-tool-use.js` sites — asserted via emitted event type and allow/deny outcome. The dual case is asserted alongside it: the run's own session with cwd inside the recorded worktree still classifies `mine` and takes the same-session branch at both sites.
2. `resolveRun` with a session id never returns `attribution: 'session'` for a run whose recorded worktree is a different live worktree than the caller's cwd.
3. Every existing `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` and hooks-suite assertion passes without modification — single-session behavior is byte-identical.
4. Reverting the pre-tool-use/context changes (keeping the new tests) makes the new tests fail.
5. Full `npm test` green.

## Technical Approach

Both sites already have `ctx.cwd`/`ctx.input` in scope — construct the caller identity once per check, call the predicate, and map its three verdicts onto each site's existing branches. In `resolveRun`, apply the predicate only inside the `owner === me` arm (the `unowned` fallback arm is #607's territory and stays untouched). Do not add new event types or messages; the fix is purely which existing branch fires.

### Data / API Surface

No new exports. Verdict→branch mapping at the two pre-tool-use sites: `foreign` → existing foreign branch; `mine` → existing same-session branch; `indeterminate` → each site's existing fall-through (teardown: the collapsed deny; commit: `wd-deny`) — an unowned-but-bound target run whose binding doesn't contradict the caller classifies per the predicate's table (typically `indeterminate` from the main checkout, `mine` from inside the binding), landing in the same branches those inputs reach today. In `resolveRun`'s loop: `foreign` → skip; `mine`/`indeterminate` → return (current behavior). No new denials are introduced anywhere — `indeterminate` maps exclusively onto branches that already fire for those inputs, so the hooks contract's never-break-a-session invariant is untouched.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — the two comparison sites
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `resolveRun`'s session-scoped arm
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` (+ the resolveRun-covering hooks suite) — new sibling cases

## Gotchas

- The commit-path's deny (`wd-deny`) for same-session wrong-place work is a *feature* — a sibling reclassified as foreign gets allow+warn, which is the designed cross-actor behavior. The safety invariant "cwd inside the recorded worktree ⇒ `mine`" is a requirement on the prerequisite's predicate (its table's second row), restated in AC1's own-session test case here — not an assumption to eyeball.
- Scope of the worktree-binding proxy: it distinguishes **isolated-worktree** siblings — the incident class. Two same-session actors sharing one worktree (or both in the main checkout) are indistinguishable to the predicate and classify per its same-cwd rows; that residual is accepted and documented, not solved here.
- Worktree-path recycling: a terminal run's dir is reaped/archived by reconcile, but a stale *non-terminal* run recording a since-recycled worktree path is the pre-existing exposure, unchanged by this record — the predicate adds no secondary run-id check, and none is in scope.
- `indeterminate` must not accidentally take the foreign (allow) branch on the teardown path — its current behavior there is deny, and loosening it would weaken E-checks, the opposite of this record's intent.
- #976 (git-plumbing gate bypass), #750 (friction-lens false positives), and #703 all touch `pre-tool-use.js`; #607 touches `resolveRun`'s fallback arm — check merge overlap before building, and keep this unit's diff surgical to the two comparison sites + one loop arm.
- Byte-pinned prose/conformance suites exist repo-wide — run the full suite before merge, not just the hooks files (byte-pinning tests fail only at the merge combination).

Surface: backend

## Overview

Harden the five mutating run-state verbs in `plugin/bin/hooks.js` (`close-run`, `record-worktree`, `record-pr`, `spec-status`, `teardown-run`) against sibling-agent stomps: unknown-flag rejection, an unambiguous-only implicit fallback, and a write-time ownership guard built on `classifyOwnership` (prerequisite sub-issue). Extended under the #965 decomposition (see the parent record's Decision Rationale): the original remedy this record mandated — hard-require `--run` and remove the fallback — was considered and rejected during the #965 brainstorm in favor of unambiguous-only resolution, which keeps the one-session-one-run interactive case working while making a foreign stomp structurally impossible. This record's Deliverables and Acceptance Criteria below supersede the original ones.

## Original incidents (preserved)

- During a `/dispatch` firing, a Task-tool build/review subagent working on #860 omitted `--run` on one `record-worktree`/`close-run` call. The CLI fell through to its "newest non-terminal run" fallback and silently overwrote a LIVE sibling session's `run-state.json` (an unrelated, actively-in-use run for #758, different session, process still running) with `worktree:null`/`status:clean`/the wrong `sessionId`. The corruption was recovered manually; the original `sessionId` could not be recovered.
- #965 (2026-08-19/20): a mistyped `close-run --help` — not a known flag, silently ignored by `resolveRunArg` — fell through to the same fallback and overwrote spec-315's run-state three separate times, from three different sibling worktrees. All three siblings shared the parent session's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (measured 2026-08-20), so `closeRunState`'s session-id-only foreign check read the victim run as "mine".

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 7

## Non-Goals

- No change to `pre-tool-use.js` E-checks or `resolveRun`'s attribution — that is the enforcement-layer sibling sub-issue.
- No change to explicit-`--run` semantics: an explicit `--run` on a foreign run still proceeds with the advisory line (console execution and post-merge settlement depend on this override).
- No change to read-only verbs (`resolve-run-dir`, `reconcile`, `archive-run`'s own validation, etc.) beyond what the shared `resolveRunArg` seam carries.
- No removal of the implicit fallback for the genuinely unambiguous case — that rejection is recorded in the parent's Decision Rationale.

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| 1098 | hooks context: add classifyOwnership (#1098) | open |

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — `resolveRunArg(args, cwd, env)` (shared by all five verbs): looks only for `--run`; anything else silently falls through to `ctxLib.resolveRunDir(cwd, env)` — called WITHOUT a sessionId third argument, so resolution is the pre-#62 "newest non-terminal run" guess. `record-worktree` (writes `worktree`/`status`/`sessionId`), `record-pr`, and `spec-status` have no ownership check at all on the implicit path.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/close-run-state.js` — `closeRunState(runDir, { explicit, sessionId })`: refuses an implicit close only when `prev.sessionId !== sessionId` — defeated by the shared session id. Also consumed by `teardown-run` (`teardown-run.js` passes `opts.sessionId` through).
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `resolveRun`'s env-first (`PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`) resolution; `findRunByWorktreePath`; `classifyOwnership` (from the prerequisite sub-issue): composite identity — a run's owner is `{ sessionId, worktree binding }`, a caller is `{ CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, cwd }` — returning exactly one of `'mine' | 'foreign' | 'indeterminate'`; `foreign` means provably another actor's (different session id, or same/missing id with the caller's cwd in a different live worktree than the recorded binding). The prerequisite's Data / API Surface table is the verdict contract; verify the shipped signature matches it at build start. A run with **no** worktree binding classifies `indeterminate` (or `mine` from the main checkout with equal ids) — never `foreign` — which is what makes the fail-open asymmetry below work.
- Tests: `tests/hooks-dispatcher.test.js` covers these verbs' current fallback behavior (its no-`--run` cases are also non-hermetic against an inherited `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` — #1038).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Known-flag declaration per verb at the `resolveRunArg` seam: any `--*` argument not in the verb's declared set prints that verb's one-line usage and exits without reading or writing any run state. `close-run --help` must become a usage printout. The declared sets (source of truth: a `KNOWN_FLAGS` table in `plugin/bin/hooks.js` beside the handlers, consumed by `resolveRunArg`): `close-run`: `--run`; `record-worktree`: `--run`; `record-pr`: `--run`; `spec-status`: `--run`, `--spec`, `--status`, `--phase`, `--now`; `teardown-run`: `--run`, `--merged`, `--abandoned`.
- [ ] Implicit resolution (no `--run`) for the five mutating verbs replaced with the unambiguous-only order: (1) `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` env — kept first, but no longer exempt from the write-time guard below (an *inherited* env var reaching a foreign run is a documented pollution vector, #1038; only explicit `--run` overrides a `foreign` verdict); (2) cwd-binding reverse lookup via `findRunByWorktreePath` on the caller's cwd — a hit is the caller's own run even with N siblings live; (3) after excluding candidates whose `classifyOwnership` verdict is `foreign` (verdicts `mine` and `indeterminate` both remain actionable — an unbound run may still be the caller's, the fail-open asymmetry), exactly one candidate remains → act on it; (4) otherwise refuse, listing **every** non-terminal candidate — foreign ones included, annotated `(recorded by another session/worktree)` so the operator sees why they were excluded — each as a paste-ready `node "<plugin>/bin/hooks.js" <verb> --run "<dir>"` line.
- [ ] `closeRunState`'s `foreignOwner` predicate upgraded from the raw session-id comparison to `classifyOwnership` (implicit and env-resolved paths refuse on `foreign`; explicit `--run` proceeds with the existing advisory). Signature: `closeRunState(runDir, { explicit, callerIdentity })` with `callerIdentity = { sessionId, cwd }` replacing the bare `sessionId` option — exact option naming at implementer's discretion, but both callers (hooks.js `close-run`, `teardown-run.js` Step 1) must thread cwd through.
- [ ] `record-worktree`, `record-pr`, and `spec-status` refuse an implicit write when the resolved run's `classifyOwnership` verdict is `foreign`, with the same refusal shape (message naming the run, its owner evidence, and the paste-ready explicit command).
- [ ] Named regression test, fixture pinned exactly: **four** non-terminal run dirs; callers A, B, C each cwd'd in their own worktree with their own run bound to it; run D bound to a fourth worktree whose agent is absent; all four runs record the same `sessionId`. Each caller invokes `close-run --help` (must hit the unknown-flag usage path — zero state reads/writes) and bare `close-run` (must hit resolution step 2, its own cwd-bound run). Assertions: run D's `run-state.json` ends byte-identical in every case; each caller's bare `close-run` closes only its own run. **Unbound-caller variant** (the #860/#758 incident shape, where the stray caller may have had no bound run): a fourth same-session caller cwd'd in a worktree with no bound run invokes bare `close-run` — step 2 misses, step 3 excludes A/B/C/D as `foreign` → zero candidates remain → refusal (exercising step 4), and no run-state file changes. All spawns clear `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` explicitly (the #1038 hermeticity fix applied to these new cases from the start).
- [ ] Update `tests/hooks-dispatcher.test.js`'s existing no-`--run` cases to the new semantics, clearing `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` in every spawn env.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the five verbs, given any undeclared `--*` flag (`--help`, a typo), prints usage and performs zero reads/writes of any `run-state.json` — asserted by fixture-file mtime/content equality.
2. Bare `close-run` with exactly one non-terminal candidate remaining after the foreign-exclusion filter acts on it (current interactive behavior preserved; one foreign + one non-foreign candidate therefore acts on the non-foreign survivor); with two or more surviving candidates, or with zero survivors (every candidate foreign, or none at all), it refuses and the refusal output contains one `--run` command line per non-terminal candidate, foreign ones annotated.
3. A caller whose cwd is inside worktree A can never implicitly resolve, close, or overwrite a run bound to worktree B, even with identical `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` — the named regression test above proves the incident shape is dead.
4. Explicit `--run` on a foreign run still proceeds, printing the existing advisory (`closing run … recorded by another session`) — byte-compatible with today's message.
5. `record-worktree --run <dir> <path>` (the sanctioned, documented call shape) behaves byte-identically to today.
6. Bare `record-worktree <path>` (no `--run`) with two or more non-terminal runs present, or with its only candidate classified `foreign`, refuses without writing — the verb that creates bindings has no cwd-binding step-2 hit for a first-time record (its target is unbound at call time), so only `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` or the single-surviving-candidate rule can resolve it; this AC pins that carve-out so a future edit to the shared resolution order can't silently regress it.
7. Full `npm test` green; reverting the hooks.js/close-run-state.js changes (keeping the new tests) makes the new tests fail.

## Technical Approach

Extend `resolveRunArg` to take the verb's known-flag list and return an `unknownFlag` field the caller turns into the usage line; thread a `callerIdentity = { sessionId: process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, cwd: process.cwd() }` object into the implicit-resolution path and the write guards. The unambiguous-only candidate scan reuses `iterRunDirsWithState` (newest-first) exactly as `resolveRun` does — do not build a second run-dir enumerator. `record-worktree` note: it *creates* the binding, so at call time its target has none — implicit resolution for it can only succeed via `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` or the single-non-foreign-candidate rule; with siblings live it refuses, which makes the already-documented "always pass `--run`" discipline structural instead of prose.

### Data / API Surface

- `resolveRunArg(args, cwd, env, { knownFlags, callerIdentity })` → `{ runDir, invalidRunArg, unknownFlag, rest, explicit, candidates }` (exact shape at implementer's discretion; `candidates` non-empty only on the refusal path).
- Refusal message shape: a lead line whose wording is chosen by cause — `claude-tweaks: multiple candidate runs — pass --run explicitly:` when 2+ survive the filter, `claude-tweaks: the only candidate run(s) are recorded by another session/worktree — pass --run explicitly to act on one:` when zero survive — followed by one `node "<plugin>/bin/hooks.js" <verb> --run "<dir>"` line per non-terminal candidate (foreign ones annotated `(recorded by another session/worktree)`). Never the literal string "multiple/foreign".

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — `resolveRunArg` + the five verb handlers
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/close-run-state.js` — guard upgrade
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — read-only consumption of `classifyOwnership`/`findRunByWorktreePath`
- `tests/hooks-dispatcher.test.js` — updated cases + the named regression test (or a sibling file if it grows past taste)

## Gotchas

- The shared session id means the old guard *passes* for siblings — any test asserting foreign-refusal must use identical session ids across callers to prove the new arm, plus a distinct-id case to prove the old arm still works.
- `spec-status`'s `--run` names the multi-spec PARENT run dir (where `manifest.yml` lives), never a per-spec subdirectory — the guard must classify against the parent dir's own run-state without breaking that contract.
- `teardown-run` reaches `closeRunState` via `teardown-run.js` Step 1 — verify both entry points get the upgraded guard (one implementation, two callers).
- `mv -n`-style silent-skip lesson applies to refusals: a refusal must exit with output naming what was refused and why — never print nothing and exit 0 (the pre-existing "printed nothing, indistinguishable from success" branches in these handlers were added for exactly this reason; extend them, don't regress them).
- #953 and #761 (open) also touch `plugin/bin/hooks.js`; #457 touches `tests/hooks-dispatcher.test.js` — check for merge overlap before building.

#1179 added the Needs-human carve-out to both console files' Auto-resolution short-circuits and cross-referenced it from `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`'s Auto-merge gate. But `_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md` names a second sanctioned caller of `consoleAutoResolve`: `_shared/console-execution.md`'s reconciler-side executor, which auto-ticks and executes a PR-posted console when the ceiling is raised after render time. That file's "consoleAutoResolve wiring" section treats every console item as floor-clearing ("no narrower per-item test today") and routes execution through `review-console.md`'s "On approval" steps 1-6 — including the branch-finish/merge row — while containing zero occurrences of "merge-check" or "needs-human". Reachable scenario (traced during #1179's review): `settle-and-merge.md`'s gate fails a layer at an attended tier, so the console renders unticked on the PR without the short-circuit (and hence the carve-out) ever evaluating; nothing persists the `needs-human` verdict (`console.json`, `decisions.md` entry schema, PR label); the ceiling is later raised to `unattended`; the reconciler auto-ticks the merge box, and `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` performs no independent needs-human check. This defeats exactly the precedence rule #1179 pinned (human ruling 2026-08-21: merge-check's needs-human verdict is authoritative), via an adjacent file #1179's spec did not scope. Refs #1179.

## Deliverables

1. Persist the merge-check `needs-human` verdict at console render/post time in a place the reconciler-side executor reads (e.g. a `mergeCheckVerdict` field in `console.json` written by `_shared/console-on-pr.md`'s post procedure — mechanism choice is part of this record's design work; interaction with #347's planned per-item floor predicate must be considered, since `console-execution.md` explicitly forbids pre-implementing that predicate).
2. In `_shared/console-execution.md`'s "consoleAutoResolve wiring": mirror the #1179 carve-out — when a persisted `needs-human` verdict exists for the run, the merge/branch-finish row is not floor-clearing; Resolve stays unticked for a human; every non-merge item still auto-resolves.
3. Extend the #1179 conformance suite (`tests/console-autoresolve-needs-human-carveout.test.js`) or add a sibling suite to pin the executor-side carve-out with go-red proof, and cover the persistence mechanism with a unit test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A console posted for a run with a `needs-human` merge-check verdict cannot have its merge/branch-finish row auto-ticked by the reconciler-side executor at any later ceiling.
- The verdict survives session end (persisted artifact readable by a foreign session — not conversation state).
- Conformance/unit tests fail when the executor-side carve-out prose or the persistence write is removed.

## Technical Approach

Persist the merge-check `needs-human` verdict at console render/post time in a location the reconciler-side executor can read independent of session state (e.g. a `mergeCheckVerdict` field in `console.json`), then have `_shared/console-execution.md`'s `consoleAutoResolve` wiring check that persisted verdict before treating the merge/branch-finish row as floor-clearing — mirroring the carve-out #1179 already added to the render-time short-circuit. Coordinate with #347's planned per-item floor predicate rather than pre-implementing it. Extend or add a conformance suite with go-red proof for the executor-side carve-out and a unit test for the persistence write.

- `plugin/skills/_shared/console-execution.md` — the `consoleAutoResolve` wiring needing the carve-out
- `plugin/skills/_shared/console-on-pr.md` — the post procedure that would write the persisted verdict
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — "On approval" steps 1-6, including the branch-finish/merge row
- `tests/console-autoresolve-needs-human-carveout.test.js` — the existing #1179 conformance suite to extend or sibling

  subdirectory — i.e. `archive-merged.js`'s top-level plain-move loop (which runs before the

The materiality digest mechanism (`_shared/materiality-floor.md`, shipped by #1261) has three gaps only surfaced once real adopters (#1262) started routing findings to it — none fixable within #1262's own scope since #1262's Non-Goals bar changing the contract itself, and two require actual code (not prose).

## Current State

#1262's final whole-branch review (spec #1262, "Migrate the ten adopter files to cite `_shared/materiality-floor.md`") found:

1. **No `Defer-reason:` vocabulary for the four health sweeps' digest entries.** `_shared/materiality-floor.md`'s Entry format makes `Defer-reason: {value}` a mandatory field, and that value's vocabulary is defined by `_shared/deferral-gate.md` — but `code-health`, `docs-health`, `harness-health`, and `journey-health` never run through the deferral gate at all (they file spec-shaped issues directly via `recordPayload`/`specShapedBody`, per #1262's own Current State: "These do NOT cite the deferral gate"). There is no defined value these four sweeps can legitimately write into a materiality-digest entry's `Defer-reason:` field. #1262's own citations correctly route below-floor health-sweep findings to the digest, but leave this field unaddressed — an agent executing the sweep has no well-formed value to write.

2. **No dedup on materiality digest entries — spurious promotion after repeated firings.** The pre-existing per-origin cap digest (`_shared/health-filing-digest.md`) solves this explicitly via a fingerprint fold (`expandDigestFingerprints`) that lets a re-encountered finding dedupe against its own existing digest entry instead of re-appending. The materiality digest has no equivalent — `tidy/digest-sweep.md` has no dedup step of its own. A below-floor finding that a scheduled health sweep re-encounters on every firing gets a fresh entry appended each time; `digest-sweep.md`'s own cluster-promotion procedure fires once ≥3 entries share the same `{area}` — so a genuinely low-value, repeatedly-recurring finding becomes a first-class issue after 3 firings, inverting the contract's entire purpose (reducing issue volume for low-materiality findings).

3. **The digest comment URL and `filed/digested/cap` accounting never reach any adopter's own summary.** `_shared/materiality-floor.md`'s Deliverables state "the run's single digest comment URL... appears once in the caller's own summary output," but none of the ten adopter files' report/handoff/summary formats were updated to actually surface it, and the four health sweeps' existing `filed: N, digested: M, cap: {CAP}` throttle line (from the pre-existing cap-digest mechanism) does not count materiality-digest routings at all — so a run's actual digest activity is invisible in every caller's own output.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide and document a `Defer-reason:` (or equivalent) vocabulary answer for direct-filing producers (the four health sweeps today; possibly other future non-gate-routed adopters) — either extend `bin/lib/issues/record.js`'s closed `DEFER_REASONS` set with a value describing "no deferral gate applies, filed directly by a proactive sweep," or define an explicit, contract-stated exception in `_shared/materiality-floor.md` for this producer class.
- [ ] Design and implement a dedup mechanism for materiality digest entries — likely a fingerprint-based fold analogous to `_shared/health-filing-digest.md`'s `expandDigestFingerprints`, reconciled with `tidy/digest-sweep.md`'s existing cluster-promotion threshold so a genuinely-recurring-but-still-low-value finding does not spuriously promote.
- [ ] Wire the digest comment URL and a digest-specific count into each adopter's own summary/report format — likely ten distinct small edits (one per adopter's own summary shape) plus updating the four health sweeps' `filed/digested/cap` line to also report materiality-digest routings separately from cap-digest routings.
- [ ] `tests/materiality-floor-conformance.test.js` and/or a new suite covering the dedup mechanism and vocabulary answer once designed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A health-sweep-originated materiality digest entry has a well-formed `Defer-reason:` (or documented equivalent) value, with a test pinning it.
2. Re-running a sweep against an already-digested, unchanged finding does not append a second entry, and does not contribute toward cluster-promotion's ≥3 threshold a second time.
3. At least one adopter's own summary output surfaces the run's digest comment URL when a digest routing occurred this run; the four health sweeps' throttle line reports a materiality-digest count distinct from the cap-digest count.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Filed by #1262's own final whole-branch review — that spec's scope was citation-only (per its Non-Goals, "No change to the contract itself"); these three gaps require either a contract amendment or new code, both out of scope there. Item 2 (dedup) is closely related to #1273's existing scope (tidy's digest-sweep wiring/mechanics) — coordinate with or fold into that issue if picked up around the same time, since both touch `tidy/digest-sweep.md`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/materiality-floor.md` — Entry format, Defer-reason field, Deliverables' summary-surfacing requirement
- `bin/lib/issues/record.js` — `DEFER_REASONS` closed vocabulary (if extended)
- `plugin/skills/tidy/digest-sweep.md` — cluster-promotion mechanism, needs dedup
- `plugin/skills/code-health/filing.md`, `docs-health/SKILL.md`, `harness-health/filing.md`, `journey-health/SKILL.md` — Defer-reason gap + summary-surfacing
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md`, `wrap-up/residue-sweep.md`, `wrap-up/leftover-routing.md`, `reflect/full-mode.md`, `reflect/hindsight-mode.md`, `visual-review/browser-review.md` — summary-surfacing (these already have a Defer-reason via the deferral gate, so item 1 doesn't apply to them)
- `tests/materiality-floor-conformance.test.js`

#257 has an open draft PR #869 (build/test/review/wrap-up complete, awaiting a human merge verdict) yet was re-selected by dispatch hours after a prior firing (`2026-08-21T105702-spec-252-257-899-266-316-644-652`) explicitly released its claim on #257 for this exact reason and posted a comment documenting it. ## Deliverables

- Step 2's eligibility filter additionally excludes any candidate that already has an open PR referencing it via a closing keyword (`Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves #N`) or GitHub's native "Development" linkage.
- The exclusion is surfaced in this firing's own reporting, following the existing Blocked-exclusion report's rendering convention (`SKILL.md` Step 3) — a named line when non-empty, silent when nothing was excluded.
- All four selection forms (bare, `next`, `#N`, `#N,#M,...`) inherit the exclusion uniformly, since they all read Step 2's `dispatch-groups.json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record carrying an open PR (draft or ready-for-review) that will close it is excluded from Step 2's eligible pool, even when it still carries `auto:build` and no `bot:*` label.
- The exclusion is reported the same firing it fires, naming the excluded record and the linked PR number.
- Direct `#N` dispatch and the explicit `#N,#M,...` list form both re-check this exclusion against Step 2's live queue — consistent with how they already re-verify `auto:build`/`bot:*` there — rather than only the bare/`next` forms picking it up.
- A record with no linked PR is unaffected — no new false exclusions on the steady-state queue.

## Technical Approach

Add a linked-PR check to `queue-pull-script.md`'s eligibility pipeline, parallel to the existing `partitionByOpenBodyBlockers`/`partitionByOpenNativeBlockers` pair in `record.js`. Fetch, per eligible candidate, whether it has an open PR that will close it via the GraphQL `Issue.closedByPullRequestsReferences` connection, batched into one query across the eligible set (mirroring `buildNativeDependencyQuery`'s batching shape) rather than a per-candidate `gh pr list --search` loop. Unlike the native-dependency query, this check must run unconditionally — it isn't gated behind `work-links: native`, since PR-linkage exclusion prevents wasted re-dispatch rather than encoding a dependency-tracking policy choice.

Partition eligible candidates into `{eligible, excludedByOpenPR}` (same shape `partitionByOpenNativeBlockers` returns), write the excluded set to a new session-scoped file alongside `dispatch-blocked-excluded.json`, and thread it into `SKILL.md` Step 3's Blocked-exclusion report so both exclusion reasons render under one convention.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — add the batched linked-PR GraphQL query and partition step to the eligibility pipeline
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js` — add a `partitionByOpenLinkedPR` function alongside `partitionByOpenBodyBlockers`/`partitionByOpenNativeBlockers`
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md` — update Step 2's queue definition sentence and Step 3's Blocked-exclusion report to cover the new exclusion reason

## Gotchas

- GraphQL's `closedByPullRequestsReferences` only captures PRs using a closing keyword in their body — a PR that merely mentions the issue without one won't be caught this way; verify #257/#869's actual linkage uses a closing keyword before assuming this field covers it, and treat a non-closing-keyword mention as an open gap if so.
- The check must run independently of `work-links: native` — see Technical Approach; getting this gated wrong would silently disable the exclusion for any project not using native work-links.
- Keep the query batched across the whole eligible set in one call — a per-candidate loop repeats the same slow-fallback pattern `queue-pull-script.md` already warns about for the per-dependency open-state check.

- `node --test tests/bin-lib/declined-learning/store-concurrency.test.js` passes reliably across multiple consecutive isolated runs (not just once).

## Technical Approach

Start with `plugin/bin/lib/declined-learning/store.js`'s `recordDecline` and its lock-acquisition/write-then-release sequence — confirm whether two workers can both read a stale snapshot before either writes (a lost-update race), or whether the test's own worker-spawn/timing assumptions are the actual source of flakiness.

- Reproduce first with several isolated `node --test` runs of just this file before concluding root cause — the observed 2/3 failure rate in isolation argues against pure machine-load flake, but confirm before assuming a real lock bug.

## Current State

`_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s canonical entry schema and `test/verification.md`'s reporting guidance do not require a test-gate decision-log entry that names specific failure causes to account for every failure in a stated count.

Observed on #994's wrap-up: the first of that group's two `/flow` calls wrote a `decisions.md` Step-4 test-gate entry stating "8 fail" and naming 6 of them by category (chmod-based permission tests, installed-plugin version mismatch, two remote-dependent reconcile tests) — silently omitting the other 2 (`impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js`'s `gatherSignals()`/CLI-entrypoint failures, "could not resolve an installed root at the pin" — environmental, Impeccable not installed in that sandbox). The omission was invisible to a reader trusting the entry; it surfaced only because the second call independently re-ran the full suite from raw output instead of trusting the prior claim, per that dispatch's own explicit "re-derive from artifacts, never a prior claim" instruction.

Why was this possible? The entry's author enumerated known/recognized failure categories from experience with the suite rather than tallying named causes against the log's actual `not ok` count. Why did that go unnoticed? Neither schema requires a partial-enumeration summary to account for 100% of a stated count, or to fall back to "N failures, see full log" when it can't. Reproducible on any future decisions.md entry anywhere in the plugin that summarizes a multi-cause test-gate result this way — systemic, not a one-off.

## Deliverables

1. Add a line to `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s canonical entry schema (or `test/verification.md`'s reporting guidance, whichever more directly governs test-gate entries) requiring: a decision-log entry that names specific failure causes must account for every failure in the stated count, or state the count with "see full log at {path}" instead of a partial named list that could be mistaken for complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A future decisions.md test-gate entry either enumerates every failure by name/cause, or explicitly signals the enumeration is partial / points to the full log — never a bare partial list with no signal of incompleteness.

Surface: backend

## Overview

Plan Audit (`/build` Common Step 1.5, procedure in `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md`) is executed by the model following prose — deterministic path checks and greps hand-run at plan time, a per-run cost in both context and reliability. Mechanize the deterministic checks into a Node CLI, `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js`, and shrink `plan-audit.md` to invocation, result interpretation, and policy handling. Adds a fourth deterministic check — size-headroom for near-ceiling files — absorbing #553 outright and the check half of #641.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 8

## Non-Goals

- Judgment checks stay prose in `plan-authoring.md` (deictic re-resolution, degrade-clause convention, #734's gate-over-producers) — they are not mechanically checkable
- No change to Common Step 1.5's skip-gate conditions in `build/SKILL.md`
- No change to scope-creep policy resolution or the interactive prompt (both remain skill-level interpretation)
- No insertion-size estimation in the headroom check — v1 reports current bytes + headroom only; projecting a planned insertion's size is unreliable and the plan author judges borderline cases
- #641's pr-early-run-lifecycle merge-time half (re-scoped into #641's remainder after this lands)

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| #257 | build: pre-dispatch verification pass over each task's own stated acceptance command | **Hard block — do not start until #257's PR merges.** Check C's field shape is pinned from its merged diff (never its issue text) as this record's first plan task. |
| #897 | build: extract plan-authoring checks and Common Step 2 dispatch detail into lazy-loaded sub-files | **Hard block — lands first.** Current State's byte figures and check locations here are pre-#897/pre-#257 and must be re-derived from the post-merge files at plan time. |

## Current State

(Figures below are as of 2026-08-18, pre-#257/pre-#897 — re-derive at plan time.)

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` (4,585 B) — Check A (every `Files:` path exists, or parent dir for Create), Check B (`Scope keywords:` repo sweep listing matched-but-unplanned files), the `scope-keywords-required` policy row, the auto-mode `scope-creep` policy table, and the interactive three-option prompt. #257 (in flight) is adding a Check C (per-task acceptance-command pre-check) to this same file.
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` Common Step 1.5 — the skip gate (fewer than 3 file references AND no `Scope keywords:`, or `ceremony-profile: fast-lane`) and the summary; the gate must stay decidable without loading `plan-audit.md`.
- Plan format: plans are written by `/superpowers:writing-plans` to `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}.md`; there is no formal grammar for `Files:` sections or the `Scope keywords:` field today — this CLI's test fixtures become the first formalization (see Technical Approach).
- `plugin/bin/` conventions — multi-file modules live in `plugin/bin/lib/{name}/` as flat sibling directories (never a nested `_shared/`); `resolve-policy.js` is the policy reader. #892 (`bin/verify.js` — deterministic verification runner + `verification.md` migration) is the same mechanization pattern for a sibling skill file, `ready` but not started: no dependency, but align output-envelope conventions with it if it lands first.
- Ceiling constant: 40,960 bytes — `CEILING_BYTES` sourced from `context-cost.js`, pinned separately by `tests/bin-lib/harness-health/skill-md.test.js`; its governed set is the skill corpus (`plugin/skills/**/*.md`). Reuse the constant; never restate the literal.
- #553 (closed as superseded by this record): asked for a Check A warning when a plan adds prose to a file near the 40 KB ceiling. Incident behind it: #535's plan specified a 636-byte insertion into a file with 349 B of headroom, caught only at the final whole-branch review.
- Tests: `tests/bin-lib/{module}/` suites are auto-discovered by `npm test`'s recursive glob.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Plan task 0: pin Check C's field shape from #257's merged diff — recorded in the plan before any implementation task
- [ ] `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js` — CLI taking a plan file path: Check A (path existence / parent-dir-for-Create), Check B (scope-keyword sweep, matched files absent from the plan), Check C (per the pinned shape from task 0), Headroom (for each existing file the plan adds prose to: current `wc -c` and headroom against the ceiling constant — files in the constant's governed skill-corpus set plus any other `.md` file the ceiling test covers; scope pinned in task 0 alongside Check C)
- [ ] Structured output: JSON envelope with per-check status + offending paths, plus a one-line human summary
- [ ] `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` rewritten: CLI invocation, result interpretation, policy handling only — no hand-run grep/ls procedures for the mechanized checks
- [ ] `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/` — fixtures: missing path, unswept scope keyword, near-ceiling file, already-breaching file, a Check C failure per its pinned shape, clean plan. The near-ceiling fixture's test carries a comment naming #553 (so a future edit surfaces the supersede coupling)
- [ ] `build/SKILL.md` Common Step 1.5 invokes the CLI (skip gate untouched)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fixture plan naming a missing `Files:` path → Check A failure naming that path, exit non-zero
2. A fixture plan whose `Scope keywords:` match a repo file absent from the plan → Check B failure naming that file, exit non-zero
3. A fixture plan adding prose to a governed file with < 1,024 B headroom → `nearCeiling` soft flag naming the file, its current bytes, and remaining headroom; exit 0 when nothing else fails (the flag is informational — the skill layer surfaces it per policy)
4. A fixture plan adding prose to a file already at/over the ceiling → `breach` entry, exit non-zero
5. A clean fixture plan → no failures, no flags, exit 0
6. A Check C fixture exercising its pinned failure shape → the corresponding structured failure, exit non-zero
7. The headroom check derives the ceiling from `context-cost.js`'s constant, not a repeated literal
8. `npm test` green; the near-ceiling test names #553 in a comment
9. `plan-audit.md` contains no hand-run procedure for Checks A/B/C or headroom

## Technical Approach

The CLI parses the plan markdown for `Files:` sections and the `Scope keywords:` field, then checks paths via `fs` and sweeps keywords via an fs-walk — never a gitignore-honoring grep, so gitignored-but-relevant files can't silently vanish from a sweep. Exit non-zero when any check fails (`nearCeiling` alone does not fail); the skill layer maps failures onto the existing scope-creep policy / interactive prompt.

**Parser grammar:** no formal plan grammar exists — the fixtures ARE the contract. The parser tolerates: `Files:` or `**Files:**` labels; `-` or `*` bullets; backticked or bare paths; one path per bullet line; `Scope keywords:` as a line-anchored field. Derive the tolerated shapes from real plans in `docs/superpowers/plans/` and encode each in a fixture.

**Walk scope:** rooted at `--repo-root`; excluded: `.git/`, `node_modules/` (any depth), `.claude/`, `.claude-tweaks/`, `evals/node_modules/`. `--repo-root` defaults to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the cwd, falling back to the cwd itself outside a repo.

### Data / API Surface

- `node plugin/bin/plan-audit.js <plan-path> [--repo-root <path>]` → stdout JSON: `{checkA: {ok, missing: []}, checkB: {ok, unplanned: []}, checkC: {…pinned from #257's merged diff in plan task 0}, headroom: {ok, nearCeiling: [{file, bytes, headroom}], breaches: [{file, bytes}]}}`; exit 0 iff every check `ok` (with `nearCeiling` entries allowed)

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js` — new CLI entry
- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/` — module files when multi-file (flat sibling dir, per `plugin/bin/lib/{name}/` convention)
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` — rewrite
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — Common Step 1.5 invocation wording
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/` — new suite

## Gotchas

- Re-read #257's landed diff FIRST (Prerequisites hard block) — pin Check C from what actually merged, never its issue text
- Recursive grep honors `.gitignore` (ugrep) — Check B must use the fs-walk with the stated exclusion set, plus a control match in tests, or gitignored-but-plan-relevant files audit as clean
- `grep -c` counts lines, not occurrences — occurrence assertions need `grep -o | wc -l` semantics
- Sweep/check matching: case-insensitive and content-anchored; count mismatches in fixtures are usually fixture bugs, not code bugs
- The ceiling is pinned twice today (`context-cost.js` + the harness-health test) — import, don't triplicate

## Decision Rationale

See #896 (parent) — mechanization follows extraction (#897) because headroom is the enabler, and mechanizing the deterministic checks is the strongest fix for the instruction-efficacy finding (prose checks the model can route around become exit codes it cannot).

## Current State

`categoriseReproduction` (`bin/lib/coordination.js`) requires severity-bucket agreement (`high`/`critical` vs `medium`/`low`/`info`) between two reviewers before treating a finding as reproduced. A run's own lens-3c reproduction pair agreed on location and substance for the digest-vs-Approve finding (`step-6-auto.md:154`) but rated it high (B) vs medium (A) — straddling that bucket boundary. Because of the strict bucket-agreement rule, a substantively reproduced finding came back `unconfirmed` and needed a direct-verification override to be rescued. A pair that agrees on the defect but straddles the high/medium line is a common shape; the bucket rule turns it into a false negative that only a source-reading reviewer catches.

## Deliverables

Change `categoriseReproduction` so a location+substance agreement with a straddled severity bucket is treated as reproduced (severity contested) rather than dropped to `unconfirmed` — e.g. take the lower of the two severities as the confirmed value, or flag the finding explicitly as "reproduced, severity contested" rather than silently downgrading it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reproduction pair that agrees on location and substance but rates severity in different buckets (e.g. high vs medium) is classified as reproduced, not `unconfirmed`.
- The confirmed severity for such a pair is deterministic (e.g. the lower of the two) or the "contested" state is surfaced explicitly to whatever consumes `categoriseReproduction`'s output.
- Existing reproduction-pair test cases that both agree on severity bucket keep their current classification (`reproduced` when they agree, `unconfirmed` for genuine location/substance disagreement) — this is a narrowing of the false-negative case only, not a general loosening.
- `npm test` green.

## Technical Approach

Locate `categoriseReproduction` in `bin/lib/coordination.js` and its severity-bucket comparison logic. Add a location+substance-agreement check that, when true, short-circuits the strict bucket-equality requirement and instead resolves severity via the lower-of-two rule (or an explicit "contested" flag), consumed by `skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s reproduction-pair handling.

### Key Files

- `bin/lib/coordination.js` — `categoriseReproduction`

## Gotchas

- Don't loosen the rule for pairs that disagree on *location or substance* — only the specific case of agreement on both with a straddled severity bucket.

## Current State

#647's expand phase shipped per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` (`permittedGrants`), fixing a bug where the flat top-level `reason` string could pair a granted `bornReady` with the other grant's denial text. The flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys were kept as a transitional twin, with the module header (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, lines ~10-15) recording a removal condition: delete the flat keys at the first release on or after 2026-11-16 (ship date + 3 months, per `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape).

Two skill-text consumers carry a matching read-side fallback, tagged with the same removal condition: `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (line ~144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (line ~223), both doing `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }`.

Confirmed at shaping time (2026-08-17): the module header text, both fallback call sites, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line (`↳ trust: {provenance} / {band} — {verdict}{, {coverage}% coverage}`) all reproduce exactly as described — the trust-table snippet's `bornReady`/`reason` output fields (written to `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) are genuinely dead: nothing downstream reads or renders them.

The removal date (2026-11-16) has **not** yet passed as of this record's shaping (2026-08-17) — it is roughly three months out. This record documents and prepares the contract phase; it does not authorize building the removal before that date.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Verify, at build time, that the current date is on or after 2026-11-16 (the first release on/after that date) before making any of the changes below. If built before that date, stop without editing anything and report the record as not yet actionable — see Acceptance Criteria #1, a hard gate.
- [ ] Re-run `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` to confirm every consumer still reads only `grants.*` shapes (no new flat-key consumer introduced since shaping).
- [ ] Remove the flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys from `permittedGrants`'s return value in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, and delete the module-header comment block documenting the now-resolved removal condition.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (the `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` pattern and its explanatory comment), reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (same pattern, same treatment).
- [ ] Drop the dead `bornReady`/`reason` output fields from `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet (the `node -e` block that writes `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) — confirmed nothing downstream (`skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line) reads them.
- [ ] Decide, and record the decision inline as a code/skill-text comment, how to handle the two disclosed conflation residues before deleting the flat keys:
  1. Withheld grants share one reason string today — `grants.bornAuthorized.reason` can carry born-ready's rationale on the human-filed path. Decide whether this stays as-is (the per-grant shape already fixes the *granted*-path pairing bug; the withheld-grant sharing is a separate, lower-severity residue) or gets its own follow-up record.
  2. The granted path's flat `reason` today carries positive rationale text ("class is clean, ceiling is unattended, grant origination opted in") that no per-grant key reproduces. Decide whether to populate that positive rationale into the granted per-grant `reason` field, or record explicitly (in a code comment) that it is intentionally dropped as noise once the grant itself is visible via `granted: true`.
- [ ] Update or remove the flat-key compat tests in the `bin-lib/issues` test suite to match the per-grant-only shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hard precondition, checked first:** the build only proceeds once the current date is on or after 2026-11-16. A build attempted before that date stops without modifying any file and reports the record as not yet actionable — this is not a normal "build failed" outcome, it is the record's own documented gate.
2. `permittedGrants` (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`) returns only the per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` shape — no flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys at the top level.
3. No consumer (code or skill text, across `skills/` and `bin/`) reads the flat keys or carries a fallback for them — confirmed via `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` read against every hit.
4. `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet no longer computes or emits `bornReady`/`reason` fields.
5. The two conflation-residue decisions are recorded (as a comment near the code they affect, or in this record's own close-out note) — not silently dropped.
6. `npm test` passes with the flat-key compat tests updated or removed.

## Technical Approach

Start with the grep re-verification (Deliverables item 2) — the module header itself calls this out as the first step, since a consumer could have appeared between #647 shipping and this record's execution.

`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`: delete the flat keys from `permittedGrants`'s two return objects (denied-path and granted-path, around current lines 128-155) and the header comment block (lines 10-15) documenting the removal condition — the condition is satisfied, not evergreen.

`skills/capture/SKILL.md` (~line 144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (~line 223): drop the `|| { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` fallback half of each destructure, reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly; delete the accompanying "older installed build" comment.

`skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table `node -e` block (~lines 219-234): remove `bornReady`/`reason` from the `out[issue.number]` object literal.

Fold the two conflation-residue decisions into the same edit pass — they're small text/comment changes, not separate work.

Grep the `bin-lib/issues` test directory for `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized` flat-key assertions on `permittedGrants`'s return value and update/remove them alongside the source change, in the same commit.

## Gotchas

- **Date gate is load-bearing, not advisory.** This record was shaped on 2026-08-17, roughly three months before the 2026-11-16 backstop. Confirmed by reading `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`'s own module header, which states the removal condition explicitly and cites `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape as precedent for this pattern (see also #628/#629, which apply the same shape to `policy.yml` key retirements). Marking this record `ready` reflects that it is *shaped* and *queued*, not that it is *buildable today* — `/specify` has no mechanism to hold a record out of `ready` pending a future calendar date (only `parked` + `Trigger:` does that, and only `/tidy`/`/wrap-up`/`/reflect`/`/review`'s Defer paths can add it), so this Gotcha and Acceptance Criterion 1 are the only gate. Whoever dispatches this record (`/flow`, `/build`, or a human) must re-check the date before touching code.
- **Information loss is real if the conflation residues are skipped.** Deleting the flat keys without deciding the two residues (the Deliverables item above them) silently drops the granted-path's positive rationale text — no per-grant key reproduces it today. This isn't a formatting nit; a human reading a future trust/grant explanation loses the "why" for a clean grant unless this is deliberately decided and recorded.
- **Verified against live code at shaping time**, not taken on faith from the issue text: read `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` lines 1-40 (module header and `permittedGrants`), `skills/capture/SKILL.md` line ~144, `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` lines ~203-235, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md` lines ~75-100 (the rendered trust-consequence template, confirming it never references `bornReady`/`reason`). All three deliverables reproduce exactly as the original request states — no false premise to correct here.
